text:
Ruth: Quick peek: small-viewport charts hide legend labels when "compact legend" + smoothing are enabled. Support says users can't discover hidden items with keyboard or screen readers. Thoughts?

Diego: We should avoid moving DOM order. Proposal: keep fixed legend height + 'Show all' toggle that reveals remaining items inline. Make the toggle a real button with aria-controls.

Aisha: Accessibility: when toggled, emit an aria-live polite string: 'Legend expanded: 3 additional series visible'. Also add aria-hidden on visually muted items only for assistive tech if we truly want to hide them from SR (but prefer keeping them for context).

Nolan: Microcopy idea: button label "Show all series" (tooltip "Reveal hidden legend items"). Short visual label could be "Show all". Keep action verbs.

Ruth: Visual hint: gradient fade at bottom + small button flush to chart border. CSS should respect prefers-reduced-motion. Example: .legend-fade { height: 28px; background: linear-gradient(transparent, var(--bg)); }

Diego: Implementation note: use roving tabindex inside the legend list so tab stops remain compact. Arrow keys move focus between items. Ensure screen reader still gets announcements when focus moves.

Aisha: For screen readers, also announce counts on chart state changes: e.g., 'Chart updated: smoothing enabled; 2 outliers hidden; legend collapsed: 4 items visible, 2 hidden.' That context prevents confusion about missing spikes.

Nolan: Tests: keyboard nav for toggling, aria-live snapshot for collapsed->expanded, and visual snapshot for fade+button. I'll add them to legend.test.tsx.

Ruth: Action items: Diego prototype toggle + roving tabindex; Aisha add aria-live templates to a11y checklist; Nolan add tests; Ruth will finalize copy and tokens.
